title: Microbatch floor thresholds and staged KV compaction to sustain QPS spikes
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: During abrupt QPS spikes some nodes repeatedly oscillate between small microbatches and full eviction cycles of the KV cache. This causes GPU memory churn, increased kernel launch overhead, and a sharp rise in 99th percentile token latency and OOM warnings.

Goal: Implement a multi-pronged runtime-level mitigation: (1) a microbatch "floor" (minimum microbatch size) tunable that reduces pathological tiny-batch churn under bursty traffic; (2) staged KV compaction that separates low-impact opportunistic compaction from high-priority eviction under pressure; and (3) an admission-scoring heuristic to demote or reroute low-value requests during transient overloads. The combined approach should keep tail latencies within SLO during 2x-5x short spikes while reducing forced evictions and GPU memory fragmentation.

Success metrics (targeted):
- Reduce KV eviction rate during simulated 3x QPS spike by >= 40% vs baseline.
- Keep token p99 latency increase <= 20% and absolute p99 <= 800ms for generation workloads used in the canary.
- Eliminate OOMs / kernel failures in the spike window.
- No more than 5% throughput regression in steady-state (non-spike) traffic.

Non-goals: full redesign of the batching scheduler or KV data format. This is an operational mitigation and runtime knobs release, not a model-level change.
acceptance_criteria: Microbatch floor configurable per-route and per-model; default set to adaptive policy (see implementation notes)
Staged KV compaction implemented with two modes: opportunistic-background and pressure-driven-foreground
Admission scoring prototype emitting per-request decision (accept/demote/reroute) and corresponding metrics
End-to-end canary run (10% traffic) with synthetic spike shows eviction reduction >= 40% and p99 within target
Docs and runtime CLI flags added; telemetry dashboard panels for eviction-rate, compaction-time, admission-decisions, and headroom fractions
Automated e2e rollback if GPU mem OOMs observed in canary (>0 within 1h window)
implementation_notes: Microbatch floor: add lower-bound to microbatch admission algorithm (configurable per pool). If admission below floor, queue until either floor reached or latency budget expires (configurable). Implement two modes: 'static-floor' and 'adaptive-floor' (adaptive uses decaying EWMA of recent batch sizes and GPU headroom to adjust).

KV compaction: implement compaction tokens limiting concurrent compactions per-GPU. Add opportunistic compaction that runs when GPU headroom > 25% and request rate low; pressure-driven compaction triggers immediate selective evictions using recency-weighted priority (favor evicting entries with low reuse probability estimated from recent fingerprint hits).

Admission scoring: compute per-request weight = weighted(token_count, cache_hit_prob_estimate, route_priority). Requests with score below demotion threshold get rerouted to low-cost variant or into a background retry queue. Expose score histogram metric and a 'demotion_reason' tag for analysis.

Cross-GPU soft backpressure: extend controller to emit 'headroom_fraction' signal to router; router uses it to prefer replicas with headroom>threshold or fall back to model-quantized variant. Keep signals rate-limited to avoid feedback oscillation.

Testing: build synthetic spike harness (k6 + internal generator) that can replay production request size distribution and prefix-sharing. Add microbenchmarks to measure compaction CPU time and GPU kernel overhead during compaction. Use canary in us-west-2 on 4-node pool with mixed model sizes.

Rollout: feature flag gated; start with 'canary-10pct' for one customer pool, then 'gradual-50pct' in 48h, full rollout if metrics stable. Include automated rollback trigger for any OOMs or p99 breach > 2x baseline.

Telemetry: new dashboards: runtime/kv/eviction-rate, runtime/kv/compaction-latency, runtime/batching/avg-microbatch-size, runtime/admission/demotion-rate, runtime/headroom/fraction. Correlate with logs from allocator and kernel failure events for post-mortem.
comments: 2026-03-11 - Sofia Martinez: Spike repro harness ready (link in attachments). Observed oscillation on small 16-64 token requests causes KV eviction churn; baseline eviction-rate during 3x spike ~ 120 evictions/min per GPU.

2026-03-12 - Arjun Patel: Implemented microbatch-floor prototype (adaptive mode). Early lab run shows average microbatch size up from 2.3 -> 6.8 under spike (good). Need to measure impact on tail latency.

2026-03-13 - QA (Priya Nair): Canary plan drafted. Will run 4-hour spike at canary-10pct with traffic replay and monitor p50/p95/p99 and eviction-rate. Added smoke tests for compaction token exhaustion.
2026-03-13 - Benchmarks: initial results show eviction-rate down 35% and no OOMs in 2h run. p99 improved but p50 increased slightly (~3%). Captured traces and flamegraphs (attachments).

2026-03-14 - Design review (Ben Cho): Approved staged compaction approach; asked to add compaction concurrency cap per physical GPU to protect scheduling latency. Action: add token bucket and expose metric 'compaction_inflight'.
